output.brief: The slowdown comes from one policy change, not from Corvane or the new hires. Credit Policy v14 (effective 1 May, clause 6.3) requires a full inspection appraisal for property-secured loans above $150k. The old threshold was $500k. Those loans used to get quick desktop valuations. Full appraisals took about 8.6 days at the valuation firm, against about 1.2 days for desktop. Median valuation time for property-secured loans rose from 1.7 days in April to 7.6 in June and 8.4 in August. Full appraisals went from about 30 to about 80 a month. The valuation firm's own turnaround did not change. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, and intake, document collection, underwriting and decision times are flat. Corvane and the new hires therefore don't explain the delay. The policy change was never assessed for its effect on processing times. The rise in withdrawals is partly the system's automatic 30-day closure of inactive files, so I can't say how much of it comes from slow approvals. I'm fairly confident in this. My advice is to take the measured delay and the audit rationale (desktop valuations ran 12% high) to the credit risk committee. Don't withhold the Corvane payment, and don't put the new hires on improvement plans. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard.
